clue.text: Foreman first to resign following blunder

indicators.note: the letter from resign comes after the blunder in the answer

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

indicators.note: the first letter of the word resign is what is wanted

explanation.surface: A foreman makes a blunder and is first in line to resign over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British slang for a boss, foreman or manager.

clue.text: A simple-sounding ruler?

indicators.note: the word for simple is said aloud and its sound is spelt differently

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A riddle asking for a ruler of uncomplicated sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer (emir) is a Muslim ruler or commander.

clue.text: Licensed business that chap's established in country

indicators.note: the chap's word is set up inside the country's name

parts.note: France is a European country
his means belonging to a chap

explanation.surface: A man sets up a licensed business abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a business run under licence from a parent company's brand.

clue.text: Limitlessly extolling the grape?

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters of the word for extolling are cut off

parts.note: praising means extolling

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of the grape without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a raisin is a grape, just a dried one.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, so the grape in a later form.

clue.text: Dangerous to include 1000 in US city in prayer

indicators.note: the dangerous word takes in the city group

parts.note: hairy is informal for risky or dangerous

indicators.note: the thousand sits inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A risky move into a big American city calls for a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin; also a last-ditch pass in American football.

clue.text: Ground with a rather poor transport hub

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shabby airport that is ground-based, poorly served.
explanation.definitionFit: London's busiest airport is a huge travel hub for flights worldwide.

clue.text: Oriental character perhaps in topless DVD recording?

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word for a disc recording goes

parts.note: a DVD is a video
gram, short for gramophone, here stands for a recording

explanation.surface: An Eastern character appears in a racy disc with no top on.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol for an idea, as in Chinese script, so an Oriental character is one example.

clue.text: The Queen and her son-in-law rolling a joint

indicators.note: rolling over means the combined letters are turned back to front

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
Tim Laurence, Princess Anne's husband, was the late Queen's son-in-law

explanation.surface: Royals sharing a cannabis joint, an absurd picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint made of two angled pieces meeting at a corner.

clue.text: Return flight with Turin drop off?

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A return flight where someone drops off at Turin.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey there and back is a return flight in British usage.

clue.text: How to make barnacle bare?

parts.note: removing NACL, the chemical formula of common salt, from barnacle leaves bare; taking salt out is the process asked for

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about stripping a barnacle off a hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Sodium chloride is NaCl; strike those four letters from BARNACLE and BARE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To desalinate is to remove salt, as from seawater.

clue.text: A tough, tense, embrace

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a hug is an embrace

explanation.surface: A tough guy gives a tense embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, as a noun, is a violent ruffian or hoodlum.

clue.text: Underwear designer — his pants having poor taste

parts.note: a bra is underwear
CK is the fashion label of Calvin Klein

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of

explanation.surface: A lingerie designer's own underpants show a lack of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is slightly salty and unpleasant on the tongue.

clue.text: Greek, wild-eyed when separated, and rapacious

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed Greek, cut adrift, is grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when separated' tells you to split wild-eyed into two words: wild acts on eyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy and rapacious are synonyms for grasping and avaricious.

clue.text: Belgium — the greatest holiday destination

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: Belgium touted as the greatest place for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island famed among tourists.

clue.text: According to Spooner, ship's kitchen consumed female reptile

indicators.note: Spooner signals that opening sounds are swapped between the words

parts.note: a galley is a ship's kitchen
ate means consumed
her refers to a female

explanation.surface: A ship's galley swallowed a female reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: GALLEY ATE HER becomes ALLEY GATE HER: the hard G moves across, giving the sound of the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of America and China.

clue.text: 'Greenhouse gas discovered in NY. Roger. Out.'

indicators.note: out means wrong or confused, so the letters are rearranged
with its cover off, the word gas keeps only its middle

explanation.surface: A radio message about a greenhouse gas discovered in New York, signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger. Out.' looks like radio sign-off, but Roger is fodder and Out the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass building for growing citrus trees: a kind of greenhouse.

clue.text: Moggy: 'ERG acting strangely'

indicators.note: acting strangely signals the letters behave out of order

explanation.surface: A cat with an odd label, as if behaving strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Moggy is British slang for a cat, often a mongrel; a red-haired one is a ginger tom.

clue.text: Pure Charlie swallowed, about to bring up bile

indicators.note: around means the letters are placed around what comes next

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet
ate means swallowed

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means reading bile from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Someone pure gulps something down, then is sick with bile.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibate means abstaining from sex, hence chaste.

clue.text: Aboard pedalo, Eve rationed sunburn remedy

indicators.note: on board means the letters ride inside the following words

explanation.surface: Eve shares out the after-sun on a pedalo.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera gel is a common soothing treatment for burnt skin.

clue.text: One sleeping reportedly in sheepskin

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for a sleeper is spoken

parts.note: a napper is one who naps

explanation.surface: Someone napping inside a sheepskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Napa is a soft leather made from sheepskin, named after Napa in California.

clue.text: Last member of Cottesmore Hunt's turned up to pay respects

indicators.note: the final letter of the hunt's name is used
in a down entry turned up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a hunt's gatherings are its meets

explanation.surface: A member of the Cottesmore Hunt arrives to pay respects.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cottesmore is a famous English fox hunt in Rutland.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in regard and honour them.

clue.text: Answer American soldier bagging forbidden source of bushmeat

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the forbidden word is held inside

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier
out means not allowed, as in out of bounds

explanation.surface: A GI captures some forbidden game for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a tropical American rodent hunted for food.

clue.text: Volte-face of Universal Artists' act

parts.note: U is the British film classification for universal
a turn is a performer's act

explanation.surface: A film studio's artists do an about-face.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion, an about-turn.

clue.text: The first few clues were hard — now you can relax

definitions.text: The first few clues were hard — now you can relax

parts.words: The first few clues were hard — now you can relax
parts.note: if the first clues were hard, the remainder must be simple, and that phrase also means stop worrying

explanation.surface: A setter reassuring solvers that the tough part is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To be untroubled and stop worrying is to sleep soundly.

clue.text: Pig dropping weight, turning to muscle

indicators.note: in a down entry, the weight letter drops lower down the word

parts.note: swine means a pig

explanation.surface: A pig loses weight and turns to muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon; the word also means muscular strength.

clue.text: Brute went after this, murderously

parts.note: in Shakespeare's play Caesar's dying words to Brutus come just before Brute

explanation.surface: A savage who chased something with killing intent.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's line is a reproach to his friend Brutus as he is stabbed.

clue.text: Teen having trouble with the French perfume

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
le is French for the
scent means perfume

explanation.surface: A teenager causes trouble with French perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth between childhood and adulthood is in the age group thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Intricate patterns in part of church

indicators.note: intricate means tangled, so the letters are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: Elaborate decoration in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross arms of a cruciform church building are its two side wings.

clue.text: Detroit car test now having start postponed

parts.note: the MOT is the UK annual roadworthiness test for cars

indicators.note: the opening letter of now is put off until the end

explanation.surface: A car is tested now but its start is delayed, in the Motor City.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown, from Motor Town, is a nickname for Detroit, the car-making city.
